description_full: Euronext Athens Holding S.A. provides support services for the operation of the Greek capital market. The company operates through Trading, Post trading, Listing, Data Services, IT and digital services, and Ancillary services segments. It provides clearing, settlement, and registry services; cross-border trades; initial public offers (IPOs) and corporate actions related services; data services, including information on the cash, bond, and derivatives market; and support services for other markets, such as the energy exchange group, education, rents, and event organization services. In addition, the company operates the infrastructure for various markets, including stocks, bonds, exchange-traded funds, and derivatives; and multilateral trading facility (MTF) for smaller companies. Further, it offers a clearing platform; information technology systems and infrastructure for trading, clearing, settlement, and registry; and technological and consulting solutions. Additionally, the company engages in activities relating to the provision of central securities depository services, as well as operate as a system administrator in the Athens Exchange Clearing House. The company was formerly known as Hellenic Exchanges - Athens Stock Exchange S.A. and changed its name to Euronext Athens Holding S.A. in April 2026. The company was founded in 1876 and is headquartered in Athens, Greece. Euronext Athens Holding S.A. operates as a subsidiary of Euronext N.V.

financial_summary: Hellenic Exchanges SA is a small-cap financial services business with a $456M market cap on $95M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +35% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +6.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 36% against a 7% cost of capital — a 29-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 68% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $56M in free cash flow — roughly 59 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.69× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
